vlnmme.problem: Compare zero-shot MLLM backbones and prompt-based memory/reasoning designs using cached views instead of live rendering. The tasks cover R2R, REVERIE navigation without object grounding, and graph-adapted MP3D ObjectNav; physical control and multilingual/interactive dialogue are excluded.
vlnmme.method: A Model/Agent/Task interface and Runner load cached cardinal images, connectivity and caption metadata. Four 90-degree views are rearranged as left/front/right/back after heading quantization to the nearest cardinal direction. GPT-5 produces marker captions; BLIP-2 plus GPT-5 supplies viewpoint summaries. Two memory families use textual action summaries or an accumulating textual topological graph. Each has direct, CoT, reflection, and combined prompts. A parser extracts action identifiers and retries invalid outputs. No model parameter updates occur. Stratified subsets preserve scene/path distributions; evaluation uses standard endpoint and trajectory metrics. The cost comparison removes rendering and continuous waypoint prediction, so its speedup is framework-specific.
vlnmme.novelty: A modular simulator-free diagnostic evaluation and agent ablations, not a new continual-learning method. It makes failure inspection practical but keeps graph connectivity, cached views and generated caption inputs, which differ from physical sensors and from raw-video-only policies.

omniagent.title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding
omniagent.problem: Answer questions about long videos by selectively retrieving frames, audio or clips. The environment is a media archive with arbitrary temporal access, not a mobile robot or an unknown navigation scene.
omniagent.method: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B follows an Observation/Thought/Action loop. At each turn it reads the previous transient media plus persistent textual history, writes a textual observation and reasoning record, and calls frame/audio/clip retrieval or answer. Previous raw media are removed while timestamps and textual summaries persist. Agentic SFT uses 58,000 successful teacher trajectories from five training datasets, filtered by task outcome and GPT-4o coherence score at least 3/5. Two SFT epochs use batch 64, lr 1e-5, 16 A100s. RL uses harder queries under 300 seconds, group eight, 150 steps, batch 256, lr 1e-6, 64 A100s. TAURA normalizes trajectory rewards and multiplies each turn advantage by its mean token entropy divided by group mean turn entropy. A clipped policy objective uses these rescaled advantages, with no KL or entropy regularizer. At inference context is 64K; the prompt requests confidence at least 0.9 before answering but forces a best answer at the final step.

uot.title: Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs
uot.problem: Select useful follow-up questions when the correct answer is hidden. Evaluations are simulated 20 Questions, simplified diagnosis, and troubleshooting, not clinical deployment or embodied navigation.
uot.method: An LLM proposes candidate questions from dialogue history and a candidate hypothesis set. Each simulated answer partitions hypotheses into disjoint yes/no sets; experiments assume a uniform prior. Up to three question/answer levels form a tree. Binary answer entropy is divided by 1+abs(p_yes−p_no)/lambda (lambda 0.4 in the plotted reward) to favor balanced partitions. Rewards accumulate from root to leaf; expectation backs up using answer probabilities and uniform averaging over future generated questions. The current root question with highest backed-up score is asked. Thus future question nodes average candidates rather than maximizing a Bellman-optimal continuation. Closed-set evaluation provides the hypothesis list; open-set mode uses LLM-generated lists of 5–10 candidates and refreshes them, with three initial direct-prompt turns for 20 Questions. No model fine-tuning occurs, but repeated model calls supply simulation and a GPT-4 answerer supplies environmental responses.
uot.novelty: Information-theoretic question scoring and lookahead replace unconstrained self-evaluation in tree-style prompting. The underlying information-gain identity is standard for deterministic partitions; the sharpened reward is a heuristic and is not identical to Shannon information gain.
uot.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 GPT-4 closed-set Common SR 50.5→71.2, DX 91.3→97.0, FloDial 43.7→67.3. Open-set Common SR 48.6→55.3 while mean dialogue length slightly increases 17.1→17.4; improvement is not universal efficiency. Table 2 equal-token comparisons give pruned UoT 4.7K tokens and 20Q SR 48.1 versus adapted ToT 4.5K/33.8; full UoT 9.2K/54.4. Appendix F human audits only 10% of simulated records, finding intermediate feedback accuracy 92.9–94.4%, so simulator truth is imperfect. §5 explicitly acknowledges overlapping/noisy hypotheses and incomplete elimination. The printed Eqs. 5–6 omit entropy minus signs; Appendix A restores the intended negative entropy but an intermediate displayed algebra step drops probability factors. The final binary-entropy identity is valid under deterministic disjoint partitions; these typesetting inconsistencies should not be treated as an invalid identity.
uot.implementation: INSPECTED CODE: src/uot/uot.py:85–155 partitions candidate sets, implements the sharpened binary-entropy reward, and supports average or maximum future-child aggregation. The executable reward has the correct entropy minus signs absent from the printed equation. However, avg_expected multiplies its child average by a branch probability and expected_reward multiplies again by that branch probability (115–147); paper-equivalent expected-utility interpretation should be checked before using this implementation as a calibrated decision rule. idiv_reward also assigns reward 1 when the two partition cardinalities differ by one (103–107). These are deterministic code semantics, not evidence of benchmark impact. README includes API-dependent closed models and an open-set possibility-update protocol. cot.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
cot.problem: Improve multi-step arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic problem solving with a pretrained language model and a few demonstrations, without task fine-tuning. This is foundational prompting research, not a VLN architecture.
cot.method: Replace input/answer exemplars by input/intermediate natural-language rationale/answer triples. The model autoregressively generates intermediate tokens before its answer. Eight manually composed arithmetic demonstrations are reused across free-response datasets; AQuA uses four multiple-choice examples. Commonsense tasks use task-specific training examples, or hold out the first ten examples of evaluation-only BIG-bench tasks for prompts. Greedy decoding is used; LaMDA averages five exemplar-order seeds, while other model results use one ordering. No loss or training update is introduced. Ablations test equation-only output, dots as extra computation, and explanations after the answer. Symbolic tasks test two-step exemplars followed by longer inputs. SayCan is evaluated as language-to-action sequence generation rather than physical execution in this paper.
cot.novelty: Combines pretrained in-context learning with intermediate natural-language rationales, contrasting earlier rationale-supervised training and scratchpad/program approaches. It does not establish that a verbal rationale faithfully reports all internal computation or that longer text always improves a decision.
cot.results:
PAPER EXPERIMENT: Figure 2 PaLM 540B GSM8K solve rate roughly 18→57%; StrategyQA reaches 75.6 versus prior best 69.4. Benefits vary by scale and task; one-operation arithmetic gains are small or negative, and small models can produce fluent incorrect traces. The authors’ manual analysis includes correct final answers with invalid rationales; of 50 errors, 46% were described as nearly correct and 54% as major semantic/coherence errors. Appendix A explicitly notes parameter count is confounded with training compute. Dot and post-answer controls support usefulness of intermediate content in these setups, but do not isolate all possible extra-compute mechanisms. §6 explicitly disclaims guaranteed correct reasoning and leaves whether the network reasons as an open question.

APPENDIX CHECK: Table 7 includes negative transfers for the evaluated GPT-3 model on CSQA and StrategyQA; prompting benefits are not universal. Tables 13–19 exhibit symbol, commonsense and feasibility errors even when explanations sound coherent. The SayCan examples assume a supplied finite object/location/action inventory, and do not constitute robot execution. The supplied appendix’s correct-rationale count and the main-text count differ; this dossier uses their shared qualitative finding instead of choosing an unsupported corrected rate.

landmark_rxr.title: Landmark-RxR: Solving Vision-and-Language Navigation with Fine-Grained Alignment Supervision
landmark_rxr.problem: Coarse instruction/trajectory pairs weakly supervise individual landmarks; trajectory metrics can be dominated by where a difficult segment occurs. Landmark-RxR supplies human sub-instruction and sub-trajectory boundaries and a diagnostic reset protocol.
landmark_rxr.method:
Thirty annotators spend about 2,700 hours producing 166,740 sub-instructions and 46,645 sub-trajectories from English RxR. Each chunk has independent meaning, a changed position and clear endpoint, with cross-annotator verification. Sub-pairs, recombined adjacent pairs, full English RxR and R2R train an RCM-style encoder-decoder with ResNet panoramas and GloVe-300. Student-forcing imitation runs 100K steps, then policy-gradient training 20K, batch 100, lr 1e-4. Soft focal reward weights DTW costs at two sampled annotated critical landmarks by ten before exponentiation; hard focal reward sums +1/−1 for whether any predicted point visits each selected landmark within 3 m. The latter is order-insensitive. Diagnostic evaluation allows ten steps per landmark, then resets the agent to a failed annotated landmark and gives only the unfinished instruction suffix. This is oracle intervention, not autonomous recovery.

SUPPLEMENT CHECK: pp. 1–3 specify an RCM-like recurrent baseline and chunk granularity controls. The annotation datasheet, pp. 5–8, describes 30 annotators and about 2,700 hours, with some original English RxR instruction errors corrected. Its claim contrasting FGR2R as heuristic should be read narrowly: FGR2R uses heuristic linguistic segmentation but its released chunk-to-viewpoint alignment includes human annotation. Human landmark alignment and oracle-reset evaluation remain distinct from autonomous recovery.
landmark_rxr.novelty: Human alignment supervision and landmark-focused rewards complement global route similarity. The reset metrics isolate local competence and must be reported separately from ordinary complete-route navigation. Hard landmark reward precedes any proposal simply rewarding intermediate landmark coverage.
landmark_rxr.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 all-granularity imitation SR/nDTW 28.4/26.7; nDTW RL 29.3/43.2; soft focal 33.7/41.0; hard focal 34.9/36.6 on English RxR unseen. Thus SR and global alignment trade off. Table 2 adding fine-grained RxR pairs to R2R raises SR 33.0→40.1 while adding full pairs alone yields 33.1. Extra annotations, chunk lengths, and data volume all change; this is not a pure architecture comparison. Table 4 reset-based loss number improves 6,256→4,951 with hard focal reward, but those reset counts do not measure autonomous recovery capability. The report’s attention illustration is supportive qualitative evidence, not a causal grounding proof.

mtrack.title: One Step at a Time: Long-Horizon Vision-and-Language Navigation with Milestones
mtrack.problem: Long ALFRED household tasks fail when an agent skips a subtask or interacts with the wrong object. M-Track explicitly tracks completion of supplied low-level instructions, in addition to a high-level goal.
mtrack.method: A BERT-CRF trained on simulator-derived labels extracts milestone type and object targets. A Mask R-CNN predicts 116 object classes, masks and binary reachability within 1.5 m. WordNet WUP similarity grounds target names to reachable detections. Navigation milestones require a reachable target; interaction milestones additionally require the action mask to overlap it above IoU 0.5. A checklist tracks multiple target objects. The base LSTM or recurrent VLN-BERT sees the high-level goal and only the current low-level sentence, advancing after milestone completion. Before executing an interaction, proactive checking scans the top five predicted actions for a matching target, otherwise chooses navigation. Training combines action imitation, object selection and A2C rewards for distance, interaction correctness, visibility and final success. The VLN-BERT adaptation uses eight panoramic views and object features plus a pointer action head.
mtrack.novelty: Explicit grounded progress checks and proactive action rejection, rather than implicit attention or a learned binary switch. It is model-agnostic but the evaluated checker assumes object-centered ALFRED milestones and provided instruction decomposition.
mtrack.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 unseen LSTM-L SR/PLWSR 8.70/4.05→13.28/6.25; VLN-BERT-L 12.23/5.60→16.29/7.66. Table 3 applying M-Track only at test improves validation SR 10.35→13.29, while training and testing with it reaches 17.29. Table 4 ground-truth milestones reach 24.38, leaving extraction/grounding room. §6 explicitly states procedural instructions such as turning twice need action-history checks, implicit milestones require inference, and multiple valid subtask orders call for softer constraints. These limitations are direct prior-art statements for any proposed obligation/history tracker.
